mechanism_variables: Sympathetic reactivity index (composite z-score of EDA/HR features)
Calibration set feature density (k-NN distance in feature space)
Nonconformity score (1 - predicted probability of true class)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High sympathetic reactivity index → feature vectors land in low-density regions of calibration feature space (k-NN distance > 90th percentile) → nonconformity scores inflated relative to typical responders in same Mondrian bin → empirical (1-α) quantile underestimates true nonconformity for high-reactivity subjects → prediction intervals undercover
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between sympathetic reactivity index and undercoverage magnitude (coverage rate decreases as reactivity increases)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Calibration set size n=15 (WESAD subjects)
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class (stress/non-stress)
Reactivity threshold: top 20% of sympathetic reactivity index
Feature space: 34-dimensional physiological features (EDA, HR, TEMP, ACC)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per reactivity quantile (decile bins)
Nonconformity score distribution shift (KS statistic) between high-reactivity and typical subjects within same Mondrian bin
Calibration set feature density (mean k-NN distance) for high-reactivity vs typical subjects
Interval width vs actual error for high-reactivity subjects
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Test by stratifying WESAD subjects by sympathetic reactivity index computed from TSST response; compute per-subject coverage and correlate with reactivity.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: High gesture frequency + loose watch fit (≤3/5) → correlated motion artifacts in BVP (SQI < 0.7) and ACC → artifact pattern mimics stress signature (elevated HR, reduced HRV) → model assigns high confidence to incorrect stress prediction → Mondrian bin (predicted stress) pools clean and artifact-contaminated samples → empirical quantile inflated by clean samples → intervals undercover for artifact-contaminated subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Positive correlation between gesture frequency × (6 - watch fit) interaction term and undercoverage; coverage lowest for high-gesture/loose-fit subgroup
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: TSST task only (social stress with speaking/gesturing)
Empatica E4 sampling rates: BVP 64Hz, ACC 32Hz
Artifact threshold: BVP SQI < 0.7 or ACC magnitude > 1.5g
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per artifact severity quartile (gesture frequency × fit interaction)
Nonconformity score correlation with ACC magnitude within predicted-stress bin
Misclassification rate for high-artifact vs low-artifact subjects
BVP SQI distribution per Mondrian bin
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Use existing WESAD ACC/BVP data; compute gesture frequency from ACC peaks during TSST; watch fit not in WESAD but can proxy via baseline ACC variance.

mechanism_variables: HRV recovery slope (RMSSD change per minute post-TSST)
Cortisol recovery half-life (min, from saliva samples)
Calibration sample temporal index (early vs late in calibration window)
Feature distribution drift (Wasserstein distance between early/late calibration features)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Slow recovery phenotype (HRV recovery slope < median, cortisol half-life > 60min) → physiological feature distribution drifts across calibration window (Wasserstein distance > 0.5) → Mondrian bin pools early (near-stress) and late (recovery) calibration samples → empirical (1-α) quantile reflects mixed distribution → prediction intervals too narrow for late-phase feature distribution → undercoverage for slow recoverers in late calibration period
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between recovery speed (HRV slope) and coverage; coverage decreases for later calibration samples within slow-recovery subjects
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD protocol: baseline, TSST, recovery (~20min), meditation
Calibration window: all non-stress + stress samples pooled
Recovery phenotype: bottom 30% HRV recovery slope
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per recovery phenotype (fast vs slow) and calibration temporal half (early vs late)
Nonconformity score drift over calibration time (slope of score vs sample index)
Wasserstein distance between early/late calibration feature distributions per subject
Interval width vs actual error for late calibration samples of slow recoverers
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Requires temporal ordering of calibration samples; WESAD has sequential protocol so calibration samples have implicit time order.

mechanism_variables: Physiological arousal index (EDA tonic + HR z-score)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Low interoceptive accuracy (≤0.6) or high alexithymia (≥60) → VAS ratings mismatch physiological arousal (mismatch > 30 percentile) → Mondrian bin (predicted class) mixes truly stressed (high physiology, high VAS) and mislabeled calm (high physiology, low VAS) → true nonconformity distribution widens beyond calibrated quantile → intervals undercover for high-mismatch subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between interoceptive accuracy and coverage; positive correlation between label-physiology mismatch and undercoverage
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: VAS collected post-TSST and post-meditation in WESAD
Interoceptive accuracy/alexithymia not in WESAD (requires external measurement)
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
Mismatch threshold: top 30% of |VAS - physiology| distribution
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per interoceptive accuracy tertile (if available) or mismatch tertile
Nonconformity score distribution width (IQR) per Mondrian bin for high vs low mismatch
Label-physiology mismatch magnitude vs nonconformity score correlation
Proportion of mislabeled samples (high physiology, low VAS) per bin
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: WESAD lacks interoceptive measures; mechanism testable via simulation injecting label noise correlated with physiology, or on datasets with interoceptive data.

mechanism_variables: Stress intensity latent variable (PC1 of physiological features)
Nonconformity score (1 - predicted probability for true class)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Binary Mondrian taxonomy (predicted stress/non-stress) pools mild (predicted prob 0.5-0.7) and severe (predicted prob >0.9) stress → extreme responders (top 10% EDA tonic/HR max) have systematically higher nonconformity scores than bin quantile → rarity (n<2 per bin) prevents quantile adaptation → empirical quantile reflects mild stress majority → intervals undercover for extreme intensity
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage decreases monotonically with predicted probability within predicted-stress bin; coverage gap between mild (0.5-0.7) and severe (>0.9) > 15 percentage points
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class only
Calibration set: 15 subjects × ~200 samples each
Extreme intensity: top decile of stress intensity latent variable
Nonconformity score: 1 - predicted probability of true class
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per predicted probability decile within each Mondrian bin
Nonconformity score vs stress intensity (PC1) correlation within bin
Coverage difference between mild (prob 0.5-0.7) and severe (prob >0.9) stress
Empirical quantile vs true nonconformity quantile per intensity decile
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Directly testable on WESAD by binning calibration samples by predicted probability and computing per-bin coverage.

mechanism_variables: Skin impedance estimate (kΩ, from EDA tonic + phasic ratio)
Skin condition category (dry/normal/sweaty, from tonic level thresholds)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Extreme skin condition (tonic < 0.1µS dry or > 20µS sweaty) → EDA features shifted on manifold independent of sympathetic activity → Mondrian bin (predicted class) groups disparate skin conditions → nonconformity score distribution becomes bimodal within bin → empirical quantile falls between modes → intervals undercover for both extreme conditions
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: U-shaped coverage vs EDA tonic level: lowest coverage for very dry (<0.5µS) and very sweaty (>15µS) skin; highest for normal (1-10µS)
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Empatica E4 EDA sensor (dry electrode)
WESAD signal quality flags (may not capture impedance)
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
Skin condition thresholds: dry <0.5µS, sweaty >15µS tonic
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per skin condition category (dry/normal/sweaty)
EDA feature manifold position (t-SNE/UMAP) colored by skin condition
Nonconformity score distribution modality (Hartigan's dip test) per bin
Correlation between EDA tonic level and nonconformity score residual
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: WESAD provides EDA tonic/phasic; skin impedance not directly measured but inferable from tonic/phasic ratio.

mechanism_variables: Time of TSST start (hours since midnight)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Morning TSST (8-11am) vs afternoon (1-4pm) → higher baseline cortisol + lower HRV in morning → model trained on pooled data learns decision boundary biased toward afternoon distribution → morning subjects miscalibrated (overconfident non-stress) → Mondrian bin by predicted class fails to separate circadian groups (both classes contain mixed times) → undercoverage for morning-tested subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Coverage lower for morning-tested subjects (8-11am) vs afternoon (1-4pm) by >10 percentage points; direction depends on which group is underrepresented in calibration
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD data collection times vary across subjects (not standardized)
Cortisol samples at baseline, +20, +40, +60min post-TSST
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
Circadian effect size: baseline cortisol difference > 2 nmol/L between morning/afternoon
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per time-of-day bin (morning vs afternoon)
Baseline feature shift magnitude (Mahalanobis distance) between morning/afternoon
Nonconformity score distribution per circadian phase per Mondrian bin
Model calibration error (ECE) per time-of-day group
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: WESAD has timestamps; cortisol data available for subset. Test by splitting subjects by median TSST start time.

mechanism_variables: Feature covariance Mahalanobis distance from training population mean
Predicted probability calibration error (ECE per subject)
Subject phenotype (athlete: resting HR <50bpm; comorbid: self-report)
mechanism_builds.causal_path: Atypical feature covariance (Mahalanobis distance > 95th percentile) → model's inductive bias violated → predicted probabilities overconfident (ECE > 0.15) for these subjects → nonconformity score (1-p) too small → Mondrian binning by class does not correct feature-conditional miscalibration → intervals undercover for atypical covariance subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between Mahalanobis distance and coverage; coverage < 80% for distance > 95th percentile
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Model: gradient boosting or neural net trained on WESAD
Training population: 15 subjects leave-one-out
Nonconformity score: 1 - predicted probability of true class
Atypical phenotype: athletes (n≈2 in WESAD) or high HRV outliers
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per Mahalanobis distance quintile
Subject-level ECE vs coverage correlation
Nonconformity score vs true error calibration curve per phenotype
Feature covariance matrix distance distribution per subject
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Compute Mahalanobis distance using training set covariance; test on left-out subject in LOOCV.

mechanism_builds.causal_path: Rare phenotype (e.g., non-responders: n=2 in calibration) → few samples in Mondrian bin (n_bin < 5) → empirical (1-α) quantile upwardly biased (order statistic variance ∝ 1/n_bin) → quantile too small → prediction intervals systematically too narrow → undercoverage in expectation for that phenotype
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Inverse relationship: coverage ≈ 1-α - O(1/√n_bin); phenotypes with n_bin < 10 show coverage < 85% at α=0.1
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: WESAD calibration set: 14 subjects (LOOCV)
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class (2 bins)
Rare phenotype definition: non-responders (EDA peak < 0.1µS), paradoxical responders (HR deceleration)
α = 0.1 (90% target coverage)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per phenotype (frequency-stratified)
Bootstrap variance of empirical quantile vs phenotype frequency
Worst-case coverage across all phenotypes
Quantile bias (empirical - true) estimated via simulation
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Simulate by subsampling calibration set to vary phenotype frequency; compute coverage vs n_bin.

mechanism_variables: Baseline EDA tonic (µS) during pre-TSST rest
Coverage rate per class per anxiety group
mechanism_builds.causal_path: High trait anxiety (STAI-T > 50) → elevated baseline EDA/HR during pre-TSST (tonic > 2µS, HR > 80bpm) → non-stress calibration samples contaminated with stress-like physiology → nonconformity distribution for non-stress shifts upward → quantile threshold for non-stress bin too low → intervals undercover for true non-stress; simultaneously, stress bin quantile too high → undercoverage for stress → both classes undercover for high-anxiety subjects
mechanism_builds.expected_direction: Negative correlation between trait anxiety and coverage for both stress and non-stress classes; nonconformity gap between classes shrinks as anxiety increases
domain_specific_boundary_conditions: Pre-TSST baseline: ~5min rest in WESAD
Trait anxiety not measured in WESAD (requires external data)
Mondrian taxonomy: binary predicted class
Anxiety threshold: STAI-T > 50 (clinical cutoff)
measurable_outcomes: Coverage rate per trait anxiety tertile (low/medium/high) per class
Baseline EDA/HR elevation magnitude vs anxiety score
Nonconformity score gap between classes vs anxiety
Proportion of baseline samples exceeding stress-threshold physiology per anxiety group
mechanism_builds.mechanism_builder_notes: Testable via simulation injecting anticipatory anxiety into baseline; or on datasets with STAI-T (e.g., WESAD+).
